biography.plain_text: Carel Erwin van Asbeck was a Dutch property developer who built a business around giving historic buildings new uses. With Maarten van Dijk, he founded Victoria Lofts, whose projects extended from the Netherlands into Belgium and France. Their partnership developed apartments, offices and other accommodation in former industrial and institutional buildings.

long_biography.plain_text:
Victoria Lofts cofounder Carel van Asbeck treated preservation as part of a development's commercial appeal. In Amsterdam's former central library, his partnership retained the grand staircase and marble halls while creating apartments with mezzanines. Large communal spaces remained even though they reduced the area available for sale.

A different challenge arose at the former Stork engineering headquarters when the office market weakened during renovation. The partnership continued with well-equipped offices and shared services instead of reducing the specification. It targeted creative businesses, opened the atrium to bring light into corridors and restored the old boardroom as a meeting space for tenants.
